question: How does this approach compare to other WSD approaches employing word embeddings?

extractive_spans: GM$\_$KL achieves better correlation than existing approaches for various metrics on SCWS dataset.

title: Learning Multi-Sense Word Distributions using Approximate Kullback-Leibler Divergence
answer_short: The proposed approach uses a KL divergence-based energy function to capture entailment and distribution similarity, outperforming other WSD approaches like w2g and w2gm on benchmark datasets.
answer_rationale: The proposed approach models word embeddings as multi-sense Gaussian mixtures and uses a KL divergence-based energy function to capture both entailment and distribution similarity. It is compared with existing approaches such as w2g (single Gaussian model) and w2gm (mixture of Gaussian model with expected likelihood kernel) in experiments, showing superior performance on word similarity and entailment datasets. The KL divergence enables capturing asymmetry in entailment relations, which other models fail to address effectively.
